content:
Some of the memory chips used in Apple devices could be manufactured in the United States for the first time, if a plan involving one of the company's suppliers comes to fruition.

A new report says Apple memory supplier SK Hynix is in discussions with Intel about potentially using one of the chipmaker's planned fabrication facilities in Ohio...

According to Reuters, details remain limited at this stage, but the Korean company produces RAM and flash memory chips for Apple devices.

Some processors used in Apple devices are already produced domestically in the United States, but due to reliance on TSMC's most advanced processes overseas, these processors are only used in older models. This isn't an issue for DRAM or NAND flash chips, however, because Apple uses industry-standard versions.

However, the report notes that the plan could face opposition from the South Korean government, which, like Taiwan, may have concerns about the export of chipmaking technology, even for older process nodes.

SK Hynix said nothing has been finalized. Intel declined to comment on the report but confirmed it is continuing to move forward with development at its Ohio site.
